sources.institution: Municipalidad Provincial de Paita / CENEPRED SIGRID
sources.document: Plan de Prevención y Reducción del Riesgo de Desastres de la Provincia de Paita 2019-2021
admissible_claims: El Zanjón drains most of Paita Baja through a canal-via to the sea and overflowed during the 1983 El Niño context
Quebrada La Piscina drains toward Quebrada El Zanjón
Quebrada La Catarata drains from Paita Alta toward Quebrada El Zanjón
Quebrada Villa Naval is described as draining toward the Rada del Complejo Pesquero, with possible diversion toward Puerto Nuevo under severe El Niño conditions
forbidden_inferences: the report supplies reproducible child catchment geometry
the reported inadequate section is a measured historical hydraulic capacity for IRFEN
1983 overflow may be transferred from El Zanjón to every named tributary
Villa Naval may be forced into El Zanjón despite conflicting official topology

sources.document: Características geodinámicas en el distrito de Paita, Informe Técnico N. 0032-2021/IGP
admissible_claims: IGP identifies Nueva Esperanza, La Piscina, Catarata and Villa Naval as named ravines around Paita Baja
IGP describes those ravines as contributors whose waters ultimately flow through the principal El Zanjón drainage and then to the Pacific Ocean
IGP documents activation of Quebrada Catarata as a mudflow-producing local channel under rainfall conditions
forbidden_inferences: figure linework is a reproducible catchment polygon without an explicit georeferencing workflow
a photographed activation zone defines a full event footprint or outlet
generic rainy-season activation supplies a dated event for every ravine
the source resolves the Villa Naval outlet conflict against the municipal PPRRD
